items.title: James Lincoln Collier interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007
items.q: student called Ace Lawrence, out of a class of 150, one black, and he was immediately elected president of the class

ctx.x: I’ve known a lot of — over the course of my life obviously — a lot of guys my age more or less who were combat vets. They don’t talk about it. They just don’t. It’s too difficult in many ways. You don’t want to show off, that was another thing. And I played jazz with a guy called Flip Don Phillips who died recently. And Don I knew for twenty years. And he was in combat in France and I never knew anything about that until the last couple of years of his life. He just never talked about it. So that was the…

those sorts of things that always looked good to fraternity people. But I was a left wing guy. I wasn’t going to send this paper in. So I never — the fraternities just didn’t even know I existed, which is what I wanted. I mean I didn’t want to have anything to do with that, which I didn’t know anything about fraternities, but I just assumed they must be bad. And they were in a lot of ways. But I got up there and it turned out I had a cousin who I didn’t know, in fact had never heard of, but somebody told me you…

of the houses — Lambda Chi I guess — and it came to the final signing up and there was — he had to sign a statement saying he was a Christian. And he looked at these guys and said, “But I can’t sign this, I’m Jewish.” And they said, “Well we didn’t know and we didn’t care” but they said, “we’re stuck.” So they called up the Theta Delta House, the president, they called the president of the Theta Delta House and said, “Hey we’ve got a situation here, can you do something about it?” And so Theta Delta called the…
